description.narrative:
The Project will reduce poverty in the rural communities of 11 EDR districts through equitable and sustainable commercialization of agriculture. The project outcome will be improved efficiency of production, marketing, and processing of HVCs such as vegetables, fruits, tea, and spices in the EDR.
The project outputs include (i) increased public and private investment in commercial agriculture, (ii) inclusion of poor and semicommercial stakeholders in commercial agriculture, (iii) timely availability of market information to farmers, and (iv) enhanced capacity of project partners in supporting farmers.

description.narrative: Improved efficiency of marketing and processing high-value crops (HVCs) such as vegetables, fruits, tea, and spices in the EDR

Public and private investments in HVC marketing and processing increased incrementally Progress/Status: The value of HVCs increased by 58% and reached NRs 15,460 million. Data Source: Same as above Actual value:

Annual growth rate in HVCs increased from 5.6% (135,000 mt) in 2006 to 6.5% by project completion Progress/Status: The volume of HVC production reached to 146,968 MT, at the growth rate of 6.61% as compared to the baseline. Data Source: Same as above Actual value:

HVC exports to India and Bangladesh increased by 16% by project completion (from 54,475 in 2006) Progress/Status: The export volume of selected HVCs (large cardamom, fresh vegetables, ginger and tea) has increased by 26% (13901 MT) in 2012, compared with 2006/07. Data Source: Same as above Actual value:

Improved quantity, quality, regularity, and value of HVCs in response to market demand, and public health and environmental requirement Progress/Status: - Quantity, quality and regularity in HVCs have improved while the proportionate change is still low with regard to quality with some reasonable improvements in tea followed by vegetables and potato. - Nearly 2 out of 3 CADP target groups perceived improvements in regularity of HVCs. - In overall, value of HVCs has increased by 169% over a period of 5 years with highest increase in tea (938%) followed by vegetables (349%) and turmeric (197.5) and lowest for tropical fruits (37.3%) Data Source: - Project results-based monitoring - Project socioeconomic surveys of farmers, traders, and processors' margins and trends - National accounts - Project quarterly and annual progress reports - Project completion report Base year: 2006 Baseline value: N
